question: S032 §18 asks HCLI to make sealed-3.14 its canonical cheap resident thinker. It could not, and the reason was concrete rather than architectural.

THE_BLOCKER_WAS_NAMED_AND_IS_NOW_CLOSED.what: hcli/delegate.py default_caller talks to an OPENAI-COMPATIBLE ENDPOINT. The sealed resident is a Rust greedy example with no server, and `hawking gravity serve` wants model-*.gravity shards that DO NOT EXIST -- every Hawking body on disk is .hq30uq4, .f32v2 or .hgrafv01. That is the exact gap that has kept the fast body and the OpenAI surface from ever talking.
THE_BLOCKER_WAS_NAMED_AND_IS_NOW_CLOSED.what_shipped: tools/hcli_resident/serve_sealed.py -- /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models over the sealed binary, no second runtime invented and no change to the resident.

THE_SERVER_REFUSES_TO_START_UNLESS_DISK_.why: a shim can silently serve a DIFFERENT configuration than the seal binds -- a different artifact, a rebuilt binary, the wrong chat-template arm -- and every number downstream would then describe something nobody sealed. This session already killed a capability run mid-flight for exactly that: a rebuild changed the binary hash under a running suite.
checked_against_HCLI_RESIDENT_SEAL_json: runtime binary sha256, byte for byte
the sealed graph is the 628-dispatch one this server configures
the sealed arm is pre_closed_think, which is what this server renders
the four fusion levers it sets are the ones the seal names
THE_SERVER_REFUSES_TO_START_UNLESS_DISK_.EVERY_mismatch_is_reported_not_the_first: a reader who fixes the first of three otherwise learns about the other two one restart at a time.
THE_SERVER_REFUSES_TO_START_UNLESS_DISK_.the_escape_hatch_is_LABELLED: --allow-unsealed serves anyway and stamps EVERY RESPONSE with sealed:false, so the divergence travels with the output instead of being lost at startup.

A_SAMPLER_REQUEST_IS_REFUSED_RATHER_THAN.why: the sealed decode path is GREEDY ARGMAX. Accepting temperature and then not honouring it is how a benchmark ends up measuring a different sampler than the one it asked for -- and the seal itself records generation_config as PRESENT AND UNUSED for the same reason.

AND_THE_FIRST_VERSION_OF_THAT_GUARD_HAD_.what: the check was `body[k] not in (None, 1, False)`. In Python TRUE == 1, so `stream: true` passed the guard and the request WAS SERVED NON-STREAMED WITH A 200 -- the caller silently given something other than what it asked for, which is precisely the failure the refusal exists to prevent.
AND_THE_FIRST_VERSION_OF_THAT_GUARD_HAD_.caught_by: the mutation test, which took 13 seconds because it actually ran the model; the duration was the tell before the assertion was.
AND_THE_FIRST_VERSION_OF_THAT_GUARD_HAD_.fixed: a per-key table of acceptable values with a TYPE-AWARE comparison, so `n: 1` is fine and `stream: 1` is not, pinned by its own test separate from the parameter list because the bug was in the COMPARISON and not the list.

IDENTITY_TRAVELS_WITH_EVERY_RESPONSE.why: a caller that logs only the reply text cannot later say which body produced it -- the defect G073 found across every CAPABILITY_noetic-*.json receipt, which recorded an argparse default endpoint and no artifact identity at all.
IDENTITY_TRAVELS_WITH_EVERY_RESPONSE.and_wall_s_is_LABELLED_NOT_A_TPS_FIGURE: the binary reloads the model per call, so this is a correctness and plumbing surface and NOT a throughput one; throughput_authority names the seal explicitly in the response body.

THE_THINK_RULE_IS_THE_HARNESS_S_RULE_ON_: the sealed arm pre-closes the think block, so a well-behaved reply has none; if one appears the reply is what FOLLOWS it, and an UNTERMINATED block is an EMPTY reply rather than prose to be scored. That is capability_suite.py's rule, reused deliberately so the server and the suite cannot disagree about what a reply is -- the 2.5970-EBPW body once passed a leak check BY never finishing thinking.

tests.note: they run in 0.10 s, which is itself the evidence that every refusal happens BEFORE the model is invoked -- the version with the True==1 hole took 13 s because it did not

claim_boundary: NO REAL HCLI MISSION HAS RUN THROUGH THIS YET. The endpoint exists, refuses correctly and is tested; G083 asks for one real bounded Accelerator mission end to end with a correct verifier classification, and that is NOT done. This closes the BLOCKER, not the obligation.

ONE REQUEST AT A TIME and the model reloads per call, so this is a plumbing surface. Any throughput number taken from it would be dominated by model load and must not be quoted; the response says so in its own body.

the seal check is a HASH COMPARISON against the seal's recorded values, and the seal's own artifact_inventory_sha is NAME AND SIZE rather than content -- so this inherits that limit exactly, and a same-length edit to a weight shard is invisible to both.
greedy only. No streaming, no batching, no KV reuse across requests, no logprobs.
the server binds 127.0.0.1 and has no authentication, which is correct for a local resident and is stated rather than assumed.
next: one real bounded Accelerator mission through HCLI against this endpoint, with the verifier classification checked -- which is G083 and is what this unblocks
